response.text: Accrual and cash-basis accounting differ mainly in timing. Cash-basis records income when you actually receive cash and records expenses when you actually pay. It’s simple and shows your immediate cash on hand. Accrual accounting records income when you earn it (for example, when you deliver a product or send an invoice) and records expenses when you incur them (for example, when you receive a bill), even if cash comes later. That means accrual shows what was truly earned and spent during a period, while cash-basis shows what cash moved. Accrual gives a clearer picture of ongoing profitability; cash-basis makes it easier to track short-term cash flow. Small operations often use cash-basis for simplicity; businesses that need a fuller view of performance usually use accrual.
